solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of a message maybe despatched from 'ere

parts.note: something despatched has been sent off
'from here' is hence; dropping the H as in the Cockney 'ere leaves 'ence

explanation.surface: A dropped-H speaker sends a note off from where they stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ere tells you an H has gone: 'from here' is HENCE, and without its H that is ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A message is typically made up of several grammatical units, each one a complete statement, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Urgent message goes round in the morning to get a bit of food

indicators.note: goes round means the distress call surrounds what follows

parts.note: SOS is the urgent distress signal
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out at breakfast-time to get a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' is the container signal; the final 'a' of the clue is not part of the definition but supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried triangular pastry with a spicy filling is an example of a snack.

clue.text: Ruminate freely having abandoned motorway — what's seen in the country?

indicators.note: freely suggests the remaining letters move about into a new order
having abandoned means those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written M and I

explanation.surface: Musing in the countryside after leaving the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; 'having abandoned' it takes M and I out of RUMINATE, and 'freely' rearranges RUNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural world of plants and wildlife is what one sees out in rural areas.

clue.text: He's bad lecturing — words dissolving in big old building

indicators.note: words dissolving means the letters of those words break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A poor lecturer's words dissolve into nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'words dissolving' tells you the letters of HE'S BAD LECTURING break up and re-form.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress on its rock above Scotland's capital is an example of an imposing ancient structure.

clue.text: After tea there's huge confusion

indicators.note: after means the outsize abbreviation follows the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
OS, outsize, is a clothing-size abbreviation for huge

explanation.surface: After tea everything is in a terrible muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; OS means outsize on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter disorder is a synonym for great confusion.

clue.text: City den offering something at teatime?

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
an animal's den is its lair

explanation.surface: A city hideout serves refreshments in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The City (capitalised) is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate-topped cream pastry is a typical treat served with afternoon tea, so an example.

clue.text: US city of gold and scrap iron, so bizarre

indicators.note: bizarre means the letters are placed in a weird arrangement

explanation.surface: An American city made of gold and scrap metal, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' rearranges the letters of GOLD plus SCRAP IRON SO; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A city at the foot of Pikes Peak in the Rocky Mountain state is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Puzzle posed by leading characters

parts.note: a word puzzle in which the opening letters of each line spell out a hidden message

explanation.surface: A riddle set by the main actors of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading characters' suggests star performers, but here means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This verse form or puzzle spells a word using the initial letters of its lines.

clue.text: Make new plans for journalist — give notice about that

indicators.note: about means the word for give notice goes round the journalist

parts.note: to give notice is to resign from a job
ED, editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter quits and the plans must be redrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'that' just points back to the journalist. 'Make new plans for' is the definition, not 'journalist'.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan or draw something again in a different way is to change its plans.

clue.text: As some lines related to measurement

definitions.meaning: lines of verse can be in regular rhythm, written in a set measure
relating to the metre-based decimal system of units

explanation.surface: Some lines are described in terms of measuring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rhythmic, as of poetry, and pertaining to the metric measuring system.

clue.text: King starts to look frightened when captured by a revolutionary

indicators.note: being captured by means sitting inside the letters that follow

parts.note: a revolutionary is a Red, a communist

indicators.note: starts to look and frightened means the opening letters of those two words

explanation.surface: A king begins to look scared when seized by a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes L and F, which 'when captured by' puts inside A RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century king of Wessex, so this is an example of a king.

clue.text: Look through lines in English book that's turned up

indicators.note: in means the lines are placed inside the reversed pair
turned up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: rows are lines

explanation.surface: Skim the lines of an English book left upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's turned up' makes EB into BE; 'in' puts ROWS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a book or shop casually is to glance through it.

clue.text: Clean up something in the garden?

definitions.meaning: to clean by rubbing hard with a brush
low stunted bushes and brushwood, the kind of growth found in a garden

explanation.surface: A tidying instruction about something growing outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rub something clean and also names rough shrubby vegetation.

clue.text: We hear teacher treasures the unexpected things of life

indicators.note: we hear says the following words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a teacher is addressed as sir, and treasures are prizes; together they sound like the answer

explanation.surface: A teacher values life's unexpected moments.
explanation.walkthrough: British pupils call a male teacher 'sir'; SIR PRIZES said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unforeseen events or shocks are what the plural noun names.

clue.text: Doubling of score in match gives reason for celebration

definitions.text: Doubling of score in match gives reason for celebration

parts.words: Doubling of score in match gives reason for celebration
parts.note: a score is twenty, doubled is forty, and the match is a marriage: the fortieth anniversary is celebrated

explanation.surface: Twice the points in a sporting fixture gives cause to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'match' read as sport, but a score is 20 and a match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortieth wedding anniversary is named after a red gemstone and is celebrated by couples.

clue.text: Report of unwelcome message for sailors spells ruin

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the next words count for their sound

parts.note: jack tars are sailors, so a notice barring them is ban jacks

explanation.surface: Bad news for the navy wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacks are sailors, so a ban on them is BAN JACKS, which sounds like the answer, an Irish slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish-English slang verb means to wreck or destroy, a synonym for ruin.

clue.text: Quiet walks in York street

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ambles are leisurely walks

explanation.surface: Peaceful strolls through York.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shambles is a famous medieval street of overhanging timber buildings in York, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a well-known old lane in the city, so an example of a street there.

clue.text: Group taking a long time to provide forms of protection after accident

parts.note: a band is a group
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: A band takes forever to supply safety measures after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressings wrapped round wounds are what protect injuries after a mishap.

clue.text: People employed by recruitment agencies? They're after the tops

definitions.meaning: recruiters who poach senior executives for firms
tribesmen who took enemies' heads as trophies

explanation.surface: Recruiters chase the top people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names executive recruiters and also, literally, those who collect the heads of slain enemies.

clue.text: Lad on isle — just some handsome youth

indicators.note: just some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boy on an island is something of a looker.
explanation.definitionFit: The beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth gives his name to any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Panic ultimately increases in desperate situations

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word panic

parts.note: something that increases rises

explanation.surface: Panic eventually grows in dire times.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies or turning points of great danger are critical, desperate situations.

clue.text: Very foolish ape, silly nincompoop, tried to be flirtatious

parts.note: very foolish means mad

indicators.note: silly suggests the word ape is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a nincompoop is an ass, a fool

explanation.surface: A daft primate and a fool attempt to flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an amorous advance at someone, which is trying to flirt.

clue.text: Material couldn't be kept upright, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the preceding words are to be judged by sound

parts.note: something that couldn't be kept upright swayed

explanation.surface: Some fabric that wouldn't stand up straight, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather with a napped finish is a kind of fabric or material.

clue.text: Additional bit for one making journey

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or bill
a person travelling on a horse or bike

explanation.surface: An extra piece for a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an appended clause and someone travelling on horseback or by bicycle.

clue.text: Emissary set to return having had meal

indicators.note: returning means the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: jelly that sets is said to gel
having eaten a meal, one ate

explanation.surface: A diplomat is due back after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy or diplomatic representative is a synonym for an emissary.

clue.text: Stern man recycled the bits left over

indicators.note: recycled material is reprocessed into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A severe man recycles the leftover scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover pieces or scraps of fabric or food are synonyms for the remaining bits.

clue.text: Six together established in group

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for established sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
est. is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: Six people form an established band.
explanation.definitionFit: Six lines of verse or six musicians form a group of that size, a synonym for a sextet.

clue.text: After quiet start, one beset by terrible stress keeps going

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides by the scrambled letters
terrible implies the word stress is messed up into another order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: After a calm beginning, someone under awful pressure carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STRESS to ERSSTS; 'beset by' puts I inside it after the S, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue steadfastly is to carry on, keep going, despite difficulty.
